sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in Kingman, AZ?
sections.html:
Most Kingman sellers who want speed choose between listing with an agent and selling directly to a cash buyer, and the paperwork is the same either way. Kingman is the seat of Mohave County, so the deed recorder, the assessor, the treasurer and the courts all sit within a few blocks of each other downtown.

The city had an estimated 35,829 residents on July 1, 2025, up 9.6 percent from the April 2020 base, according to the Census Bureau. Owners occupy 68.4 percent of homes, and the median value of an owner-occupied home for 2020 to 2024 was $267,700. A five-year survey figure lags the street, so treat it as a rough anchor and ask a local agent or appraiser what comparable Kingman sales look like now.

A listing gives the widest buyer pool but depends on showings, a buyer's loan and an appraisal. A cash sale usually skips the loan and the appraisal, which shortens the calendar, though the offer reflects the buyer taking on repairs and risk. Whichever route you pick, gather these before you start:

  • Your recorded deed and the Mohave County parcel number
  • Payoff figures for any mortgage, home equity line or lien
  • Permit records for work done on the house
  • HOA or special district contacts, if the lot has any
  • The most recent property tax bill

sections.h2: What is Kingman like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Kingman is a high-desert railroad and highway town of about 37.5 square miles at roughly 3,471 feet, set in the Hualapai Valley between the Cerbat and Hualapai mountain ranges. It was founded in 1882 as a railroad siding and takes its name from Lewis Kingman, a civil engineer who supervised track building for the Atlantic and Pacific Railroad, per Wikipedia.

Buyers find Kingman through its roads. Interstate 40 and U.S. 93 meet here, with Flagstaff 147 miles east, Needles, California 62 miles southwest and Las Vegas 107 miles northwest. Postwar growth came from a former Army airfield turned industrial park and a vehicle proving ground in nearby Yucca opened in 1955, and several neighborhoods were built to house the workers.

The climate matters when you prepare a house. Kingman sits at the eastern edge of the Mojave Desert but at a plateau elevation, so summer highs rarely pass 107 degrees while winter nights often drop below freezing and snow is possible. Average yearly precipitation is about 8 inches. A storm on December 31, 2014 and January 1, 2015 left 6.5 inches of snow and closed Interstate 40 at the U.S. 93 junction for 24 hours. A buyer's inspector will look at the heating system, pipe insulation and roof as closely as the air conditioner.

About 84 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so most buyers and sellers already know the town. The median gross rent of $1,058 is a useful check if you expect an investor to weigh your house as a rental.

sections.h2: Which permits and city rules affect selling a Kingman house?
sections.html:
Work done without a permit is the item most likely to slow a Kingman sale. The city's Development Services Department runs the Building Division, which accepts applications for residential, commercial, industrial, demolition and signage work. Call (928) 753-8130 to ask about an address before you list. The division also publishes a residential permit process guide that explains the Minor Improvement Permit, which covers smaller jobs.

Inspections are scheduled by phone, and the city asks for the request before 7:00 a.m. on the day you want the inspector, with your permit number and job site address ready. If a patio cover, room addition or garage conversion was built years ago, ask the city what it has on file and what a retroactive permit would require. Fixing that before an offer arrives avoids a renegotiation at inspection.

Short-term rentals inside city limits need a city permit under Ordinance No. 1952, effective October 1, 2023. The city's rental page lists a $60 annual fee, a Transaction Privilege Tax license, a 24-hour emergency contact and written notice to neighboring homes. Operating without a permit can bring fines of up to $1,000 a month. A buyer who plans to rent by the night will ask whether your property has a permit, so be ready to say yes or no.

If the house sits outside the city in unincorporated Mohave County, a different rule can apply. State law requires a seller of five or fewer parcels of land, other than subdivided land, in an unincorporated area to give the buyer a written affidavit of disclosure at least seven days before transfer, with a five-day rescission right for the buyer, under A.R.S. 33-422.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded and taxes handled in Mohave County?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded at the Mohave County Recorder, 700 West Beale Street in Kingman, and the office lists a $30 fee for recording documents. Arizona law requires an Affidavit of Property Value to be attached to a deed that transfers title, unless the deed carries an exemption notation, under A.R.S. 11-1133. The recorder refuses a deed without one. Your title or escrow company normally prepares both, and the recorder's FAQ notes that staff cannot give legal advice on how to fill out forms.

The same page says the recorder's self-service search will show recorded liens by name, but a search does not prove the property is clear, so buyers rely on title insurance. Copies of a recorded deed cost $1.00 per page.

Property tax is billed by the Mohave County Treasurer. The Treasurer's FAQ sets these dates:

  • First half due October 1 and past due after 5:00 p.m. on November 1, moving to the next business day when that falls on a weekend. November 1, 2026 was a Sunday, so that deadline has already passed this year.
  • Second half due March 1 and past due after 5:00 p.m. on May 1.
  • Bills over $100 paid in one payment by December 31 owe no interest accrued after November 1.
  • Late payments carry 16 percent annual interest, prorated monthly.

Ask the escrow officer how the current year's tax will be prorated at closing. If you receive a bill after the sale, the Treasurer asks that you forward it to the new owner or return it to P.O. Box 712, Kingman, AZ 86402 with a note about the sale. The Assessor at 928-753-0703 can confirm the sale was recorded.

sections.h2: Who buys Kingman houses that need work?
sections.html:
Investors and cash buyers are the usual buyers for Kingman houses with deferred repairs, tenants in place, an inherited title or a looming payment problem. They price the work and the time into their offer, so expect a number below a fully repaired retail sale in exchange for speed and fewer conditions.

Compare offers on net proceeds. Ask each buyer who pays escrow and title charges, how long the buyer needs to close, whether the buyer will accept the house as is and what happens to the deposit if the buyer backs out. Get the offer in writing and read the contract before you sign. If you are behind on a mortgage, ask your lender for a payoff figure and the sale deadline first, since the calendar sets your options.

Kingman Unified School District No. 20 runs 13 schools and reports 6,734 students on its district site, and families with children will ask about the assigned school. Mohave Community College also has one of its campuses in the city.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Kingman house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, you can offer the house as is. A buyer using a loan may ask for repairs after an appraisal or inspection, while investors and cash buyers often accept a house in its current condition. Open permits and unpermitted additions can still delay closing, so call Kingman Development Services at (928) 753-8130 to check your address.

faqs.q: How long does recording a deed take in Mohave County?
faqs.a: The recorder checks each document against the recording requirements in A.R.S. 11-480 and, if it is complete and the fee is paid, assigns a recording number. Mailed originals come back in about 4 to 6 weeks, while in-person documents are returned after scanning. Your escrow company usually handles recording on closing day.

faqs.q: Do I owe property tax if I sell in the middle of the year?
faqs.a: Ask your escrow officer how the year's tax will be split between you and the buyer. Mohave County bills are due October 1 and March 1, with the first half past due after November 1. The settlement statement should show the split.

Yes, with a permit. The city requires a permit, a Transaction Privilege Tax license, an emergency contact and neighbor notice for rentals under 30 days inside city limits. Arizona law at A.R.S. 9-500.39 limits how far a city may restrict them, but a permit is allowed. The city's rental page lists a $60 annual fee.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a lien or a title question on a Kingman property?
faqs.a: Start with a title company, because the recorder's staff cannot give legal advice or do research for you. The Mohave County Recorder at (928) 753-0701 can show you how to run a basic search by name, and a title company can tell you whether liens or judgments will cut into your proceeds.
